7103411e56536a77.title: Aging disrupts sleep-driven brain fluid flow
digest: We show that cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), the liquid that surrounds and protects the brain, has reduced flow during sleep in the aging human brain.
We identified two mechanisms that contribute to this decline: disrupted sleep and impaired blood vessel function.

8ed34ba9f8956d58.title: The aging human brain exhibits reduced hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves during sleep
digest: This work shows that cerebrospinal fluid flow during sleep is impaired in the aging human brain, before the onset of any neurological disorder, and identifies parallel neural and cerebrovascular mechanisms contributing to this difference.

e6f6a222a2cd9b7c.title: Scaling productive aging to mitigate cumulative disadvantage
digest: Productive engagement among older adults — which spans employment, volunteering and family caregiving — functions as a multidimensional driver of healthspan, economic stability and social cohesion across individual and societal levels.
Here we advocate for a paradigmatic shift from observational research towards intersectional, experimental interventions designed to mitigate cumulative, life-course disadvantages.

38e9043cb95327db.title: Tracing the genetic roots of cellular identity in tumors
digest: A new Bayesian framework, Echidna, integrates bulk whole-genome sequencing with single-cell RNA sequencing to connect clonal copy-number states with transcriptional programs, providing a tractable way to ask how much of a tumor cell’s identity is encoded by its genome.

8d3a878fb3809e45.title: Aged natural killer cells get back into shape
digest: Aging natural killer (NK) cells might retain their killing machinery yet struggle to deploy it.

Liu and colleagues now link this defect to retinoid-associated lipid remodeling, and show that inhibiting fatty acyl chain elongation restores the mechanical features of NK cells that are essential for antitumor activity in preclinical models of human cancers.

42954d0f51aa14d3.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
digest: Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

3633cd280d4bf056.title: Social factors shape health as we age
digest: Our knowledge that social factors can influence health is abundant and has shaped research and policy across medicine, public health and society for decades.

In this special issue, Nature Aging features a collection of reviews and opinion articles that explore how social factors influence healthy aging across the life course and become biologically embedded.
